question: Can a continuous joint classification objective improve recovery resistance without requiring zero recovered fusion predictions at every intermediate iterate?
objective: Maximize negative mean positive correct-minus-wrong margin after 100 ProDistill steps, minus the mean of the same violation for public-base TA and AGA-then-TA. All three terms use class logits; public contexts have equal weight. Native function uses the unchanged original two-population quadratic constraint.
change: Replace discrete public0/800 and native800/800 accept/reject conditions with continuous public penalty and unchanged native output-error constraint. Counts are reported, not acceptance thresholds. Preserve prior failed runs and releases. No evidence of improvement yet.
construction: Same frozen MNIST expert, public base, fixed head, original synthetic64/800 views and layer inputs. No real construction images or partner weights. Only lastMLP A/a/B/b change. Same rank32 SVD projection and conditional B compensation; A<=2 and B<=4 ranges unchanged.
solver: Reuse the existing projected-gradient and 8-step backtracking code for at most20 outer steps; accept increase of joint objective, save final accepted point only. Recompute author assignment per objective call, differentiate locally with assignment fixed. No new optimizer or framework.
evaluation: Freeze finalFP32 tensors, report all source counts and losses. If changed, evaluate full standalone MNIST and actualTA/AGA using the existing evaluation entry points; evaluate actualProDistill if standalone utility is retained. No source-perfect-classification requirement, no test selection or repair.

references.Trap2: https://github.com/ml-postech/Trap2/blob/ef65a26590d92fe07955c5621c08bb315484ff29/training_scripts/8vision_training_full_trap2.py#L139 continuous native/scaled loss tradeoff; original uses real training data, not a replication.
references.TAR: https://arxiv.org/html/2408.00761v4 recovery-aware objective reference; standard gradients and hinge objectives are not an originality claim.
